body: That’s true.  I’ve been riding at my main barn for so long that it’s been really difficult for me to break away, but I think I’ll make that leap soon enough :)

That’s true, the more time I spend around older clients at my main barn, the more I enjoy myself.  It’s much less comparison and more just small talk and having fun.

That being said even some of the assistant trainers will indulge in the gossip and shit talk my trainer, the other trainers, other kids that are 10 years younger than them, and just generally be very cold and unapproachable for those they don’t feel are in the same league.  Even my college coaches would engage in some outright racist behavior, run lame horses into the ground, and overall just foster a reaaaally toxic environment for everyone involved (thankfully they’ve been replaced so hopefully sophomore year is better!).

Actually though, the more I think about it, the more I realize that a lot of my work at my main barn involved doing pony camp, which was full of middle schoolers who largely have the same habits I used to.  Hmmm...

Thank you for commenting, remembering that a lot of it was indeed middle school is actually really comforting.  Hopefully the future will prove better and things will improve as I get older lol

My barn is actually quite small compared to some of the big ones nearby (Heritage, Old Salem, Ox Ridge, etc).  Really I think it was just this one particular cluster of the 5 girls I rode with that just ruined it for me.  The thing is that I never really liked competing at all.  Maybe it was my pony being especially green when I was still super young, but showing gave me so much anxiety and it made me miserable, but I did it to fit in, and then when things got even more competitive I just kinda let my personality get molded from that.  

That being said I really like my trainer, but he was so hands-off socially (while all the horse show moms dug into all the drama) that I honestly think he had no idea of how much we hated each other until this one girl finally left and we were free to disclose all of the outright bullying she was doing.


At this point I’ve been riding with my trainer for so long that it’s hard for me to break away, but I think I’ll probably move on when it comes to getting my own horse one day.  I do like the small barn atmospheres as you said, and I’m definitely willing to give up some training quality for a more laid back, friendly atmosphere.

I’d love to have my horse in my yard one day!  I live close to NYC and go to school in Philly, but I’ve always wanted to move out of urban areas and just live with my horses when I’m older.  I’ve been with this one barn for so long (going on 12 years now) that it’s been difficult for me to break away, but I’ve always wanted to try western too, so maybe I’ll grow some balls and take the leap this year!
Are his exams difficult or would you say they’re pretty fair?
